text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Financial services group Achmea talks with GAK Nederland about taking over large part of GAK's operations. (p1)
- Health insurer Zilveren Kruis to start experiment with mail order pharmacy from December 15. (p1)
- Finance ministry's decision to issue a maximum of Dfl 15 billion new short term loans next year will save about Dfl 450 million in interest. (p1)
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange index AEX reaches new record high at 636.37. (p1)
- Group of investors in car dealership group Air Holdings to take court action over the company's takeover protection measures. (p3)
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel's board chairman says 1997 will be a better year than 1996, but not a record year. (p3)
- Economic affairs ministry gives Philips Electronics Dfl 105 million worth of research support this year. (p4)
- Bourse-listed realty fund Rodamco books 148 pct higher results in first nine months of 1996/1997 bookyear. (p9)
VOLKSKRANT
- Rotterdam port authority to finance 80 million guilders common carrier pipeline between Rotterdam and Antwerp in Belgium. (p2)
- Quote media sells its stake in internet provider Planet Internet to publisher De Telegraaf and Dutch PTT. (p2)
- rise in shares causes exodus of investors from bond funds. (p2)
- Amsterdam EOE-options exchange members agree on merger with Amsterdam Stock Exchange. (p19)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo threatens Serbia with boycott, if Milosevic endangers Balkans peace process. (p13)
- Potato starch cooperative Avebe seeks to improve potato farmers' income. (p29)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM invests Dfl 103 million in renovating its Boeing 747-300 fleet. (p33) TROUW
- Parliament does not agree with economic affairs minister Hans Wijers' criticism of the government audit body's report on state support for businesses. (p4)
- Flights from Schiphol Airport to get more expensive again in January. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- ABN Amro bank seeks to take over New York asset manager Weis, Peck & Green. (p11)
- Chemicals concern DSM and Polish firm Kaprolan set up 50- 50 joint-venture in Poznan. (p11)
- Engineering company Heidemij subsidiary Grabowsky & Poort gets order from Malaysia. (p11)
